newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia-Australia forum ends with historic pact.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia-Australia forum ends with historic pact.

text.p: Australia on Friday hailed as historic an agreement with Indonesia to expand economic cooperation to develop the archipelago's eastern islands, including the tourist haven Bali.

The two governments agreed during the Australia-Indonesia Ministerial Forum, which ended on Friday, to establish a sub-regional economic cooperation framework known as the Australia-Indonesia Development Area (AIDA) to boost economic ties between Australia and eastern Indonesia.

"We regard this forum as being a forum of historic importance because from this forum has emerged an agreement with Indonesia which integrates Australia in a practical economic way with Southeast Asia," Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer told a news conference.
"We see this as a very important step forward in Australian diplomatic history," he said.
Downer and Indonesian Coordinating Minister for Production and Distribution Hartarto signed the agreement at the conclusion of the two-day forum.

Hartarto said the agreement was important from the Indonesian perspective. Together with three existing regional economic zone agreements, AIDA would be a key part of Indonesia's preparations for the opening of its markets to regional free trade.
He said the private sector, including the mining industry, should play a major role in development and added Indonesian investment also would be welcome in Australia.

While Indonesia's most populous island of Java has experienced high economic growth in recent years, those in the eastern part of the archipelago still require major development to raise living standards.
The agreement sets up a special working group, which includes private sector representatives, which will work out the details for AIDA and report back to the ministers in eight months.
"In a very practical sense we believe there are opportunities that will come from it. For Australians it will mean jobs," Downer said.

The two countries, in a joint statement issued after the forum, said the meeting had allowed the nine participating Indonesian ministers and seven Australian ministers in Jakarta this week to sign or conclude eight separate agreements.
